chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is necessary to wear the turban and the burda (outer garment) on the days of Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr. As for Friday prayer, it suffices without a turban and burda.'

key_terms.يَوْمَ الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended clothing for Eid prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to establish the distinct etiquette (adab) of Eid prayers, emphasizing that wearing the turban and outer garment is a recommended act of honor and distinction for these specific occasions, unlike Friday prayer which has different requirements. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that Eid attire serves as a visible sign of celebration and communal identity, reinforcing the spiritual significance of the days through physical presentation.
